This trigger is really good, most of the time your opponent will probably have to let go of the character unless it's late game and they're pushing for game. I am giving it a 1 star buff due to the trigger, not due to the chance at countering for a Linlin character.

OP17-118.name: Rocks.D.Xebec
OP17-118.note: A vanilla 10c would have 1k counter normally. In exchange for missing counter, Rocks gets 2 effects, the first is becoming a 2k counter if you only control characters without counter. This might come up in prerelease, especially this set with so many brick characters. However, unless you're super bricked, it's probably better to save him in hand and play him when you reach 10 don. His second effect is where he gets his high grade from, On Play replacing himself in hand and playing up to 2 9c total cost differently named Rocks Pirates from your hand is a game ending effect if you're able to make use of it. If you're able to play 2 bodies with him, he's 5 stars. If you're able to play one body with him, he's 4.5 stars. If you have nothing to play with him, he's 4 stars due to him at least drawing you a card. I've averaged all 3 scenarios for his grade.

OP17-119.name: Loki
OP17-119.note: A vanilla 6c would have a 1k counter. In exchange for missing counter, Loki gets 2 insane effects. His first line of text enables all your 12c payoffs and lets you swing with him with impunity early game, turning himself into an 11k on your opponent's turn. Nothing can really threaten an 11k with normal combat as early as he comes down. Do keep in mind there is power weakening effects that are in this set and maybe he will die via non-normal combat early game. His second effect is mostly what gives him his high sccore. His On Play lets you pop any number of characters with total cost 4 or less. If you pop a 4c or 3c body, your opponent is starting the game way behind. If you pop 2 chump blockers your opponent might as well scoop it up. There are some decent 1c characters as well, so there will be scenarios where you might be able to pop 3 characters. Definitely the Secret you want to rip in your prerelease packs.

EB04-007.name: Roronoa Zoro
EB04-007.note: A 7c vanilla would have 1k counter. Zoro more than makes up for that lack of counter. You can play him on 7 don, and even if he doesn’t get character rush it’s still good to develop the body and give your leader +2k for a turn including your opponent's. If you do get the character rush online with a target to swing at, he feels super unfair. This card was incredible in the dumpsterfire that was op15 prerelease, with him being one of the culprits turning your leader into >5k alongside Holly, Fuza, Smoker, and Zeff (All characters at SR and lower). Zoro was the only one that stacked with the others, turning you into an 8k or 9k sometimes. Sorry for the PTSD reminder of prerelease that set. I was almost tempted to give him 4.5 stars due to him not always having character rush, but it’ll happen enough and him always giving the +2k is enough for me to give him the full 5.

ST32-002.name: Kouzuki Oden
ST32-002.note: A vanilla 5c would have 7k power. Oden is 1k weaker but replaces himself on play and turns one of your opponent’s characters useless for a turn. Have it be a blocker that’s annoying you, or your opponent’s best attacker that costs 6 or less, you’re really happy to play this whenever.

OP12-056.name: Monkey.D.Garp
OP12-056.note: A vanilla 8c would have 10k power and 1k counter. In exchange for 2k power and the counter, Garp offers you nothing. He sucked in his own OP12 prerelease, where you at least had a chance to play a Navy card with him. But even back then, you were going minus 3 cards from hand to get 2 bodies on board. That “best case” won’t even exist this set with no Navy cards. Garp has legitimately no upside other than to flex an SP you pulled.

P-107.name: Gol.D.Roger
P-107.note: A vanilla 8c would have 1k counter. Roger is missing counter in exchange for turning your leader into 7k if a player is at 10 don. Turning your leader higher than 5k in prerelease is an incredible effect, as we’ve seen in the past. There will be times you’re tempted to play him while neither player has 10 don. I do think there are scenarios where you have no choice, but I’m greedy and would always wait for the 10 don play. But that option does remain, which makes him a modal card. He’s either a good 8 drop when either player is at 10 don or an average 8 drop when neither player is at 10. These upsides make up for the lack of counter, but he doesn’t impact the board enough for me to push him higher than 4 stars.

OP16-098.name: Yamato
OP16-098.note: A vanilla 6c would have 8k power. In exchange for 3k power, Yamato gets a bad card selection effect and a revive effect that will never come up in this set with no 8c Black Yamatos to revive. Even in her OP16 prerelease, she wasn't good. Being able to use her activate main made her a 2 star card back then if you drew the combo. This set, without any Yamatos to revive, she is 1 star. Her On Play is selection, not advantage, and it’s not even good selection. We see draw 2 pitch 2 all the time, and she has draw 1 pitch 1.

OP14-108.name: Silvers Rayleigh
OP14-108.note: A vanilla 6c would have 8k power. In exchange for 2k power, Silvers Rayleigh gets an incredible On Play, K.O.ing a 7k power or less if your opponent is at 3 or less life. This card was amazing in OP14 prerelease, and nothing will change this set. Although his activation requirement does mean he’s not always live, in prerelease you’re likely to bring your opponent down to 3 life by the time you want to play this anyways. His trigger allows you to activate his main as well, which is annoying to lose to, and oftentimes will be worth triggering if you have another play in mind for your next turn.

ST31-004.name: Monkey.D.Luffy
ST31-004.note: A vanilla 7c would have 1k counter. In exchange for missing counter, Luffy's On Play's floor allows you to -2k power a character during your turn. Your leader and him will always be 2 cards meeting his Straw Hat requirement, and if you have more straw hats, which are common, this can minus enough power to secure a kill. If you play him on 10 don, you can give him rush by attaching the remaining 3 don, which makes him a modal card. He’s either a good 7 drop, or a really good 10 drop.

OP13-028.name: Shanks
OP13-028.note: A vanilla 10c would have 1k counter. In exchange for the missing counter, Shanks On Play refunds you all your don but doesn't let you play any more cards from hand the turn you play him. Oftentimes late game in prerelease you have a difficult choice: develop board or use your don to swing. Shanks lets you do both. In OP-13 prerelease he was one of the better SRs to get, not the best, but good enough that you were happy to see him. Do your math properly with his refunded don to secure kills on board and hits to life so that you can leave open some don for event counters, or if you don’t have any, pretend to have event counters.

P-084.name: Buggy
P-084.note: A vanilla 7c would have 9k power and 1k counter. In exchange for missing 1k power and missing counter, Buggy laughs at you for putting him in your deck. His first line of text making him not able to attack already makes him unplayable. His static effect of freezing all 3c and 4c being symmetrical seems awful for prerelease. There will be cases where you hose your opponent and freeze their weak attackers, but there will be more cases where Buggy a dead card in your hand you can’t play, since doing so will screw your board more than your opponent. And when I say dead card, he is a dead card since he has no counter. His On Play allows you to play a 6c Cross Guild from hand, but there are no Cross Guild in this set. His best case scenario lets you use 7 don to freeze 2 or even 3 of your opponents weakest attackers for the rest of the game, which might come up but it's super unlikely. The average and more likely situation is he’ll be a dead card in your hand or on field.

ST27-005.name: Marshall.D.Teach
ST27-005.note: A vanilla 7c character has 9k power and 1k counter. Teach is missing 1k power and the counter for a really good Activate Main and annoying on K.O. effect. You can kind of look at his activate main ability as an on play, since he can use it the turn he’s played, and you’re probably swinging each turn thereafter unless your opponent wants to keep dropping targets for you to pop. His on KO effect is relevant as well, discouraging your opponent from wasting swings at him lest you bring back your best black card from your trash.

EB04-061.name: Monkey.D.Luffy
EB04-061.note: A vanilla 10c would have 1k counter. Luffy is missing counter in exchange for a cost reduction effect if you're at 1 or less life and a leader buff effect in exchange for pitching a card, this effect also gives him blocker for a turn. Playing Luffy when you're at 1 life will feel great, especially if you have an event counter in hand. But Playing him on 10 don is fine too, since you still get his On Play no matter what. Unfortunately, he does not impact the board so I can't bring myself to rank him the full 5 stars. Luffy was really good in OP15 prerelease, but due to him being at Secret most people never ran into him. This set, he's SP, so even less people will have to deal with him.
